personality_one_liner: A trustworthy, clean, and structured interface that balances fintech-level clarity for payments with a premium mobility feel.

spacing.rule: Generous padding around content. Clear grouping. Use large bottom padding when scrolling behind a sticky button.

do's: Sticky header backgrounds over scrolling content

screens.name: Customer Home
screens.purpose: A dashboard focusing on the two main things a renter cares about: their current vehicle and their payment status.

states.loading: Skeleton loaders for the payment card and vehicle card.
states.empty: No active rental state: Illustration of a scooter with a 'You don't have an active rental' message and contact support CTA.
states.error: Failed to load dashboard data. Retry button centered.

screens.layout: Vertical scroll. Top section: Weekly Payment Status card (Fintech pattern: large pending amount, due date, progress bar, and primary 'Pay Now' CTA). Middle section: Assigned Vehicle card (features the scooter image, license plate, battery/status, and 'View instructions' action). Bottom section: Recent Notifications list.

screens.name: Vehicle Page
screens.purpose: Provides detailed information and usage instructions for the assigned vehicle.

states.empty: N/A - User shouldn't reach here without a vehicle.
states.error: Failed to load vehicle details. Retry button.

screens.layout: Hero layout. Top: Large edge-to-edge image of the scooter with a bottom-to-top gradient scrim. Content overlaps the bottom of the image with the Vehicle Name and Plate. Below: Specifications grid (2 columns) and a step-by-step 'How to Use' list.

screens.name: Payment Page
screens.purpose: Shows complete payment history and allows users to settle any pending weekly dues via UPI.

states.empty: Illustration of receipt. 'No payment history yet.'
states.error: Failed to load payments. Retry button.

screens.layout: Sticky top pending balance banner (if any dues exist). List of transactions grouped by month below. Each row shows Amount, Date, Status Chip (Paid/Pending/Failed), and Transaction ID. Floating Action Button for 'Quick Pay' if pending.

screens.name: Documents Page
screens.purpose: Allows users to upload and view required verification documents.

states.empty: Empty dashed bordered box to upload the first document.

screens.layout: Grid of uploaded document cards. Each card shows document type and verification status chip. A large primary button at the bottom to 'Upload New Document'.

screens.name: Admin Dashboard
screens.purpose: A command center for the business to monitor the fleet and user payments.
screens.layout: Grid of 4 top-level metric cards (Total Vehicles, Active Users, Pending Payments, Total Earned). Below: Quick action list rows (Manage Vehicles, Manage Users, Review Documents, Send Notification). Uses standard iOS list pattern with chevrons.

vehicle_hero.alt: Modern electric scooter parked on an urban street

payment_empty.alt: Shopping receipts and cash on a white background

instructions_to_main_agent: Follow 1 iOS-Native Clean personality strictly. Emphasize generous padding and structural clarity, avoiding clutter.
BANNED: Do not use any blue, indigo, violet, or purple colors. Rely entirely on the provided Moss Green brand palette and neutral grays/blacks.
Ensure the 'Weekly Payment Status' card on the Home screen uses fintech layout patterns: large monetary figures, clear status chips, and an obvious CTA.
For all images that overlap text (like the Vehicle hero image), apply a strict vertical gradient scrim (from transparent to at least 70% surfaceInverse) to ensure text contrast.
Use Phosphor icons with consistent weight (either all outlined or all filled, except bottom tabs which can switch on active state).
Do not use generic emoji for icons. Rely on the Phosphor icon set.
Keep navigation clear: Customer and Admin spaces should be completely separated by stack navigation post-login, with Customer getting bottom tabs.
Implement haptics on primary actions like 'Pay Now' or submitting documents.
Ensure 'Pay Now' buttons remain sticky at the bottom of the screen when appropriate, with proper safe-area padding.
